targetText: The landlord class, the bourgeoisie and the warlords of Japan have very serious internal contradictions, which are growing, and the lack of military co-ordination is one of the concrete manifestations of this fact.
summary: Imperialist powers are never monolithic; internal rivalries among their ruling landlord, capitalist, and military factions inevitably produce strategic blunders that revolutionary forces can exploit.
explanation: Mao identifies five major operational errors committed by the Japanese command (piecemeal reinforcement, no main direction of attack, lack of coordination, missed opportunities, and failure to annihilate), tracing them to Japan's class contradictions and troop shortages.
context: Fierce rivalries between Japanese army factions in northern and central China repeatedly prevented coordinated offensives and left vast rural areas unguarded.
